title: The cabinet grammar
one_line: An artifact's interface is part of its body — and the body's shape follows the plane you read it on.
default_finish_note: Terminal is the family default as of 2026-07-24: dark worn-metal body, signal-orange accent, green CRT screen. Every member's `@export var finish` defaults to "terminal"; pass finish="rams" for the light Braun dialect. Both finishes are gate-clean; the choice is aesthetic, not structural.

palette._comment: DEFERS TO THE KIT. These mirror HangarKit's constants so the checker and the code cannot disagree; the kit file is the source of truth. Change it there.
palette._glass_note: TWO glasses. screen (anthracite, lit) covers a READOUT — text reads AGAINST it. window_glass (pale, ~0.055 alpha) covers the PHENOMENON — balls and histograms must read THROUGH it. A milky window hides the artifact.

vertical.when: The interface plane is vertical — you FACE the artifact standing up.
vertical.silhouette: A machine: mass rises, the sign is overhead, the reading surface meets the eye.

parts.ground: back slab (shell) spanning the full body width
parts.flank: maroon side flank or side trims, full height
parts.field: window: dark backdrop + glass over the artifact's live phenomenon
parts.readout: screen inset in a service column or backboard, dark pocket + glass, ember lip
parts.controls: keypad on a WEDGE shoulder (right-triangle prism) so it never hangs in air
parts.signage: sign band in the cap, baked flush, over a full-width ember stripe
parts.service: vent slats on the shell face

horizontal.when: The interface plane is horizontal — you look DOWN at a table, deck, board or plinth top.
horizontal.silhouette: Furniture: the deck stays the deck. Nothing rises more than a hand's width above it.

parts.ground: broad working RAIL ring around the play field (the back slab, laid flat)
parts.flank: maroon EDGE INLAY — a routed LINE (~0.009 m) just under the rail's top edge, running the whole perimeter. Not a band: the vertical flank is a mass, and a mass laid flat becomes a stripe of paint. On furniture the colour is stated by a line, never by claiming the surface.
parts.field: a milled WELL the phenomenon SITS IN — a dark basin floor set below the deck plane with low inner walls, framed by the rail. NOT merely framed by the rail: a phenomenon that is only ringed hangs over open air on the legs (gradient_descent, rounded_softbody both did this). The basin floor is the horizontal translation of the vertical dialect's dark window backdrop — the surface the phenomenon reads AGAINST. And whatever the phenomenon is must START seated in the well, not spawn above it and fall (a slow-settling body reads as floating in any still).
parts.readout: screen SUNK into the far rail, ~14 degrees off the deck plane, tilted toward the reader
parts.controls: keypad recessed FLUSH in a milled pocket, face-up, pressed downward (frameless: the pocket IS the faceplate)
parts.signage: name INLAID FLAT in the near rail, read by looking down as you approach
parts.service: vents in the APRON, seen from below

translation_table._comment: Parts translate between dialects; they do not transfer. Reusing a vertical part on a horizontal artifact produces two objects pretending to be one.
translation_table.window backdrop (dark, behind the phenom: milled BASIN FLOOR the phenomenon sits in (dark plate below the deck + low inner walls) — ring alone is not enough
translation_table.inset window / screen: readout sunk in the far rail, 14 deg off the deck
translation_table.sign band overhead: name inlaid flat, read looking down
translation_table.maroon flank: maroon edge INLAY LINE under the rail's top edge (~1/6 of the edge face, not half)
translation_table.vent slats on the back: vents in the apron, seen from below

rules.name: No text outside the body
rules.check: every Label3D and baked text tag sits inside the housing AABB (inflated 0.12 m)
rules.why: The founding ruling: readouts and titles that float beside an artifact make the interface a separate object.

rules.name: The body meets the floor
rules.check: lowest element at or below y=0.06 — nothing hovers (a pedestal legitimately extends below the origin)
rules.why: A plinth, apron or skirt closes the silhouette; a hovering body reads as a prop, not furniture.

rules.name: Horizontal stays horizontal
rules.check: no HOUSING element (rail, readout, keypad, sign, apron) rises more than 0.10 m above the deck surface. The PHENOMENON is exempt — a bar chart, a loss bowl, a soft specimen may rise as tall as it needs — but it must be BASED in the basin (its low point / footing seated in the well), never hovering over open deck.
rules.why: The moment the HOUSING rises, it has become a vertical machine wearing a table. The phenomenon is what you came to see, so it may stand up — as long as it grows FROM the well and does not float above it.

rules.name: One palette
rules.check: every material albedo is within 0.02 of a canon colour, or is artifact-native (felt, dice, balls, phenomenon colours)
rules.why: Near-miss greys read as a different manufacturer. Consistency is the whole point of a family.

rules.name: Controls in the reach band
rules.check: keypad centre between 0.75 m and 1.35 m ABOVE THE FLOOR CONTACT (not above the artifact origin)
rules.why: VR ergonomics: below is a crouch, above is a stretch. Measured from where the artifact meets the floor, because the fix for a low keypad is a PEDESTAL (HangarKit.plinth, built downward from y=0) — the face is already right, the object was simply too low.

rules.name: Screens are seated, not floating
rules.check: each glass panel has a dark pocket within 0.03 m behind it
rules.why: A pocket makes a screen inset; without it the glass is a poster taped on.

rules.name: The ember line
rules.check: at least one emissive accent element present
rules.why: The family's signature: one warm line in a cool machine.

rules.name: Compose the kit, don't retype it
rules.check: the artifact's .gd references HangarKit (source-level check in check_cabinet_grammar.py)
rules.why: Every hand-rolled box is a chance to drift. The station props look manufactured because they share one vocabulary; a bespoke cabinet cannot stay in family by memory.

members._note: registry name softbody_gallery_part2 resolves elsewhere; the upgrade landed on rounded_softbody.gd. rounded_softbody_test.tscn is a TEST HARNESS (own camera+light) and must not be the member — a harness in a map is the demo-as-artifact UI leak.

process: 0. LOOK at the good ones first: /props-dna-gallery second half (the station family) and /cabinet-gallery.
1. READ the artifact: which plane is its interface on? That picks the dialect before anything else.
2. PICK the body type from that dialect's list, or name a new one.
3. COMPOSE HangarKit — finish_palette, box, readout, bolts, stencil, three_color_bar, grime_band. Never re-type its geometry.
4. BUILD from the dialect's parts — never from another dialect's parts.
5. RE-HOME the live text into the housing; retire floating titles (the signage owns the name).
6. CAPTURE and look. The capture is the gate, not the code.
7. CHECK: python tools/check_cabinet_grammar.py — every element measured against the rules above.
8. RECORD: if the improvement has a reach, write its class-condition in doc/transfer_ledger.md.

kit._ruling: THE CABINET IS NOT BESPOKE. commons/artifacts/_hangar/hangar_kit.gd already carries this family's vocabulary — its readout() docstring names cabinets as a client, and its signage() exists so text 'reads as PART of the artifact rather than floating beside it', which is the founding ruling, implemented before I hand-rolled it five times. The station props in the second half of /props-dna-gallery look manufactured because they COMPOSE this kit. Build from it; do not re-type its geometry. And check for a KIN idiom before assuming the kiosk: a jar is a specimen, not an appliance. Palle 2026-07-20 pointed at lab_specimen_4cf36 — the containment tank in surreal_lab's specimen mode — which is the correct ancestor for any vessel artifact.

vocabulary.finish_body(finish, c, wear): the housing surface — wear darkens and roughens
vocabulary.box(center, size, mat): the box helper; hand-writing MeshInstance3D+BoxMesh is the smell
vocabulary.readout(header, lines, size, bg, text, h: the framed instrument screen: matte bezel, lit face, coloured header
vocabulary.signage(header, lines, size, reach, dir,: a bracketed sign — text mounted ON the artifact
vocabulary.stencil(text, size, color): the asset code (GB-01). A machine carries a unit number, not only a title
vocabulary.dust_streaks(w, h, z, count): age — never over a window, it reads as smears on the phenomenon
vocabulary.plinth(w, d, h, finish, wear, accent, co: a pedestal built DOWNWARD from y=0 — raises an artifact into the reach band without touching a single authored coordinate; auto-grounding does the lift
vocabulary.wedge(w, h, d_bottom, d_top, mat): the sloped shoulder a control pad rests on — vertical dialect only; the horizontal dialect recesses its pad flush instead
vocabulary.specimen_dock(base_r, dock_r, base_h, co: the containment-tank idiom for a specimen you can still LIFT OUT — tapered base, lit cradle ring, strut cage to an OPEN collar, readout inset in the base. A dome would seal shut a pickable specimen, so the dock omits it.

kit.gotcha: grime_band/dust_streaks bake their Z into position — assign .position.x/.y only. grime_band is an OPAQUE dirt shadow: it belongs at the BASE of a light body where dirt collects, never floating mid-body and never on a dark face (it reads as a hanging slab) or over a window (smears on the phenomenon). And derive the near-black 'dark' from a fixed value, not panel.darkened() — 0.55 lands at ~0.31 grey and washes out every pocket, plinth and apron in the family. grime_band is also a FLAT plate: on a cylindrical body it juts out as a slab instead of lying on the surface — round bodies take their age from banding (light mid-section between dark collars) and bolt rows instead.
